chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Bobby Tucker takes the job; the pros and cons of accompanying
summary: Tucker, who envied his steady job, has been with Eckstine ever since, while Malachi says accompanists rarely get to play.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: That was when he got the pianist that he has now, and he's been with him ever since -- his name is Bobby Tucker. A fine pianist and a fine arranger and musician. He and I are good friends. Bobby went with him in early 1948, and has been right there ever since. And it's so funny, Bobby Tucker had been Billie Holiday's pianist. When we used to play on 52nd Street... As a matter of fact, the last time we played 52nd Street, he was not with Billie Holiday. He was working with a group that Babs Gonzalez had at the club where we were working, in the Onyx Club, and he was playing piano. They had a little trio, quartet I believe it was. And I was there, working as Billy's accompanist. So a lot of times, I would ask him if he'd let me sit in with the group. And he'd tell me all the time, "Man, I wish I had your job." I said, "Accompanying a singer?" He said, "Yeah."

Accompanying a singer is fine, but the only thing about it, when you're working accompanying a singer, you never really get a chance to play, other than just the accompaniment that you do. When we came on, Billy was introduced and I accompanied him, and that was all the playing I would do. So whenever I wanted to play, I would have to go sit in with somebody.
So that was a thing that we had. He laughed all the
time. I said, "The grass is always greener on the other side. You want this, and I'd like to be where you are."

Anyway, when I left, Bobby took the job, and apparently he liked it, because I don't think Bobby has played with an instrumental group since then, and every time I see him, he seems to be quite comfortable with job. And that's 35 years that he's been there. So any time you're on the job that long, there's got to be something about it that you like.
